newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank association warns against EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: German bank association warns against EMU delay.

text.p: The Federation of German Banks (BdB), Germany's largest banking association, on Saturday warned against delaying the launch of Europe's single currency beyond the January 1 1999 deadline.

BdB managing director Manfred Weber told German radio he feared significant upheaval on financial markets should European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) be delayed, particularly with regard to the deutschemark.
"That would be poisonous for the German economy," Weber said.
"I do not see that one can simply postpone the euro, nor do I see the necessity to do so," he said.
Weber said he was optimistic that Germany could fulfil the criteria for monetary union.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel's insistence on a strict 3.0 percent deficit to gross domestic product ratio was not part of the Maastricht Treaty, he said.
